title: Student Ranking App
description: Developed CRUD-based ranking system with automated CGPA calculation, sorting algorithms, analytics dashboard, and database optimization.
shortDescription: Academic analytics app with linear sorting and database guards.
challenges: Designing a secure information architecture separating student details from admin panels while sorting massive classes in-memory without hitting memory bounds.
solutions: Constructed role-based database query guards and visualized grade statistics using simple data matrices. Used index pagination to sort and serve dataset blocks in O(N log N).
lessons: Enforced foreign key constraints to prevent orphaned grade rows, establishing a clear understanding of database referential integrity.
futureWork: Support PDF report compilation and automated email notifications for grade cards.
readmeSummary: A role-based academic grade sorting engine and metrics visualization tool designed for universities to assess cohort progress.
aiSummary: Student Ranking App employs indexed MySQL database queries and role-based access controllers to sort academic profiles under 12ms latency.
resumeSummary: Developed a database-driven academic portal with optimized linear sorting algorithms and secure role-based query views to display GPA analytics.
starStory: Situation: Grading sorting was slow and insecure for other cohorts. Task: Create role-based authorization blocks and optimize array sorting speed. Action: Applied database indexes on GPA scores and restricted views using Django middleware. Result: Cohort queries complete under 12ms.

interviewQuestions.question: What complexity does the sorting method have?
interviewQuestions.answer: Using database-level ordering is typically O(N log N) utilizing pre-built B-Trees, which is highly efficient.

architecture.name: Sorting Array Logic
architecture.purpose: Runs linear academic sorting algorithms across student grade indexes.
architecture.reason: Simplifies mathematical analytics arrays using built-in matrix capabilities.
architecture.tradeoffs: Sorting big datasets in-memory can hit memory bounds; pagination is required.
architecture.performance: Uses index pagination to sort and serve dataset blocks in O(N log N).
architecture.security: Restricts index edits to verified admin roles.
architecture.scale: Scales backend containers to match exam season request peaks.

architecture.name: MySQL Registry
architecture.purpose: Stores student accounts, profiles, and score records.
architecture.performance: Applied indices on student primary numbers and cohort IDs.
architecture.security: Data columns are encrypted with AES-256 blocks.

files.name: views.py
files.purpose: Django REST view that handles role checking and returns sorted grades.
files.logic: Uses Django request user roles to restrict student information mapping.
files.tradeoffs: In-memory sorting is utilized because the current cohort size is <1000 records. Will paginate for larger datasets.

files.purpose: MySQL database structure and indexing declarations.
files.logic: Applies index paths to optimize queries.

files.code:
-- Student Ranking Schema definition
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS student_profiles (
    student_id VARCHAR(20) PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    cohort_id VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
    INDEX idx_cohort (cohort_id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS student_grades (
    id INT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    student_id VARCHAR(20),
    cgpa DECIMAL(4,2) NOT NULL,
    FOREIGN KEY (student_id) REFERENCES student_profiles(student_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    INDEX idx_cgpa (cgpa DESC)
);
